card.name: Verbs and pronouns about what we produce or use
card.fires_on: Short verbs, pronouns or possessives right after a subject such as we, you or it, in general web prose about resources, production and what people have or do. It sits on the word that continues a clause about making, using or getting something.

modes.label: Verb after we
modes.description: A verb after 'we' in statements about waste, building or what is known.
modes.example: Environment Canada says we<< throw>> away 4 million disposable diapers a day

modes.label: Pronoun or object in resource talk
modes.description: A pronoun or possessive in sentences about energy, supply or guidelines.
modes.example: According to a study by Greenpeace, the world could produce 95 per cent of the electricity<< it>> needs from sustainable sources within 40

modes.label: Noun about output or staffing
modes.description: A noun for production or new workers in a sentence about totals.

card.writes: It mostly pushes Chinese words and odd name pieces up and customer-service or company words down, so it has no clear effect on English text.
card.plain: It fires on small words in everyday sentences about what we make, use, have or throw away.
